key_insight: HERMES++ unifies 3D scene understanding and future-scene generation in a single driving world model, enabling both accurate semantic/ geometric perception and predictive simulation of scene evolution.
problem_solved: Bridges the gap between semantic reasoning (e.g., LLM-style interpretation) and physical simulation by providing a single model that jointly understands 3D driving scenes and predicts their future geometric evolution, reducing the mismatch between interpretation and generation.
method: Learn a shared spatio-temporal 3D representation that encodes semantics and geometry from multi-sensor inputs (e.g., lidar, cameras).
Joint training with combined objectives for 3D scene understanding (semantic/instance/geometry) and generative future prediction to align perception and simulation.
Modular architecture: multimodal encoder → dynamics-aware predictor (temporal/physics priors) → decoder/generator that produces future 3D scene frames and semantic outputs.
impact: Provides a practical foundation for safer, more consistent autonomy stacks by consolidating perception and prediction into one model—simplifying integration, improving long-horizon planning, and enabling richer simulation for testing and evaluation.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing encoder (sensors) → shared 3D latent → dynamics predictor → generative decoder
Side-by-side sequence of 3D scene snapshots (past → predicted future) to illustrate geometric evolution
Bar/line chart comparing unified model vs. separate perception+generation baselines on key metrics (accuracy, consistency, long-horizon error)
Icon set for modalities (camera, lidar), semantics (bounding boxes/labels), and simulation (timeline/playback) to emphasize multimodality and application
paper_title: HERMES++: Toward a Unified Driving World Model for 3D Scene Understanding and Generation
paper_authors: Xin Zhou, Dingkang Liang, Xiwu Chen, Feiyang Tan, Dingyuan Zhang
